question: On 20 August 2025, Parliament announced that it was filing a case with the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) against the Council. The action challenges the use of Article 122 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) as the legal basis for the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) instrument1, which was adopted on 27 May 2025.

Using this legal basis deprives Parliament of its right to scrutinise sensitive matters. While the SAFE instrument, as part of the ReArm EU programme, is intended to rapidly strengthen the European defence technological and industrial base (EDTIB), the Commission’s decision to bypass democratic oversight has called into question the legal certainty of the instrument, disregarding the institutional balance.

On 9 September 2025, the Commission published the provisional allocation among Member States of the EUR 150 billion in loans provided under this instrument with the aim of enhancing defence preparedness among Member States. In this context: 1.
How does the CJEU referral affect projects financed by the SAFE instrument, and what steps is the Commission taking to secure them?
To restore transparent cooperation with Parliament and enable proper oversight, will the Commission provide full details of SAFE funding commitments? If so, according to what schedule?
Does the Commission intend to invoke Article 122 TFEU again for other components of the ReArm Europe plan?
OJ C 326, 26.10.2012, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/treaty/tfeu_2012/art_122/oj.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.2.2026) The European Parliament has initiated legal proceedings before the Court of Justice of the EU to annul the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) Regulation1 under Article 263 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU).

This legal challenge does not trigger the suspension of the SAFE Regulation from being implemented since the European Parliament requests the court to maintain the effects of the contested act until its replacement with an act adopted on co-legislation basis.

The implementation of SAFE is progressing and on 30 November 2025 the Commission received the European defence investment plans from 19 Member States and an assessment is being undertaken before proposing Council implementing decisions. The SAFE Regulation establishes reporting obligations from the Commission to the European Parliament and the Council on the use of the financial assistance.

The reporting will be on an annual basis starting in 2026. Furthermore, the Commission will perform information and communication activities related to SAFE involving where appropriate the European Parliament. For exceptional cases, it is necessary to preserve an interpretation of Article 122 of the TFEU which allows the EU to act swiftly in various situations of emergency.

The use of Article 122 does not confer autonomous powers on the Commission; rather, it allows the Commission to propose measures which the Council can adopt under strictly defined and exceptional circumstances. In the case of SAFE, it is a temporary urgency measure with a very specific purpose.
The Commission, therefore, considers Article 122 as an emergency Treaty mechanism, anchored in solidarity and necessity, whose activation must remain justified and exceptional.
